question: Should QQBot permanently reject gateway messages above 1 MiB, accepting that an over-limit event closes the socket and is not delivered?
rationale: The dependency mechanism is correct, but neither current OpenClaw behavior nor the cited QQ protocol documentation establishes 1 MiB as the channel contract; choosing the ceiling balances memory hardening against compatibility and message delivery.

options.title: Accept 1 MiB ceiling
options.body: Approve the submitted bound as appropriate for QQ JSON gateway envelopes and explicitly own the rare over-limit disconnect and event-loss behavior.

options.title: Use a larger ceiling
options.body: Raise the fixed bound, such as to the 16 MiB precedent used by some sibling transports, to retain substantial hardening with more compatibility margin.

options.title: Pause for contract evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until QQ production telemetry or authoritative platform documentation establishes a defensible maximum event size.

recommendation.title: Accept 1 MiB ceiling
recommendation.body: Approve the submitted bound as appropriate for QQ JSON gateway envelopes and explicitly own the rare over-limit disconnect and event-loss behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their major QQBot gateway architecture work makes them the strongest available owner for the channel-specific payload policy.
